region: Lodi · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Silver Thread is a small winery on Caywood Road in Lodi, three-quarters of a mile off Route 414 on the east shore of Seneca Lake. Richard Figiel planted its first vines in 1982 and farmed them organically, fermenting with native yeasts. In 2011 the winery passed to Paul Brock, formerly winemaker at nearby Lamoreaux Landing, and his wife Shannon, previously wine director at the New York Wine & Culinary Center. The Brocks kept the name and plantings and still run it themselves, making about 3,000 cases a year.

The Brocks describe their farming as biointensive viticulture, a holistic, regenerative approach to soil and vine health, aiming for sustainability rather than strict organic certification in the humid Finger Lakes climate. The winery draws all of its electricity from a 28-kilowatt solar array on site. Gewürztraminer, the perfumed grape of Alsace, suits this cool lakeside setting, which keeps its aromatics lifted. The 2021 is made dry and light, at just over 11% alcohol.

The winery’s note describes exotic aromas of lychee and acacia blossom leading to a silky texture, with a palate that is surprisingly light, dry and delicate for a grape that can run heavy and sweet elsewhere. Silver Thread suggests it with a wide range of foods, and its restraint and gentle perfume make it a natural partner for the kind of vegetable-forward, wood-fired cooking where a more opulent Gewürztraminer might overwhelm the plate.
